content:
Talia Benson: Got AWS Marketplace reviewer feedback back via portal (not a hard reject, but they want edits before approval). Posting verbatim-ish summary + assigning owners.

Talia Benson: 1) Listing copy: they flagged a few phrases as “unverifiable / too absolute”
- Remove/soften “guaranteed lowest latency” (they want measurable + contextual). Suggest: “optimized for low latency and high throughput”
- Remove “HIPAA-ready” mention (we weren’t claiming HIPAA compliance formally, but it appears in one bullet in the long desc)
- They want a clearer separation of Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private: right now the long description reads like one SKU does everything.

Soojin Lee: Ugh, knew “guaranteed” would get dinged. I’ll adjust copy + re-upload the long description block today.

Camila Reyes: +1 please make sure the headline doesn’t imply performance promises we can’t prove in listing.

Talia Benson: 2) Security attachments: they’re asking for clarification on 3 items
- Encryption at rest: explicitly state which storage layers are encrypted and whether customer-managed keys are supported (they said “KMS mention is vague”).
- Audit logging: they want a sentence distinguishing “platform audit logs” vs “customer app logs” + retention window.
- Data retention: they want the retention language to be consistent across listing FAQ + security packet. Reviewer called out “30 days” in one place and “configurable retention” in another.

Marcus Lin: I can take the encryption + audit logs wording. We should avoid implying customer-managed keys are available in Hosted if it’s only for Private/VPC.

Dr. Aisha Rahman: Please route final security language to me before resubmission. Also: SOC2 report handling needs NDA disclaimer; AWS often asks but we cannot attach the full report publicly.

Olga Petrov: Re: SOC2: we can attach the “SOC 2 Type II bridge letter + attestation” in the portal, but full report only via controlled share. I’ll draft the approved language + what’s attachable.

Talia Benson: 3) Screenshots: they require updated screenshots with these specifics
- Must show the “Set up / Onboarding” page without any customer data. No real org names / no tokens.
- They want 1 screenshot that shows “usage / cost breakdown” but with all identifiers redacted.
- The architecture diagram needs a legend (control plane vs data plane) and region boundaries called out.

Elliot Price: For docs screenshots, we have a staging env with “Redwood Demo Org” + fake projects. I’ll coordinate with Design (DES-212 owners) but I can also do a quick capture if needed.

Connor O'Brien: Reminder: anything in portal needs to match what we’re launching. Please don’t upload screenshots of UI behind flags unless we’re confident the flag will be on at launch.

Lauren Bishop: For Dedicated vs Private separation: do we want AWS listing to present separate “plans” as separate SKUs, or just keep the one listing and indicate optional add-ons?

Talia Benson: Reviewer didn’t force multiple listings, but they asked to “make the purchased product clear” and not describe unavailable deployment modes in a way that looks included. My read: keep one listing page, but the copy must align to the SKU being purchased (and use “available with Dedicated/Private” qualifiers).

Vivek Kulkarni: That aligns w/ how we’re packaging Private anyway. For AWS, Private is a separate contract/SKU in portal; we just need to avoid making it sound like Hosted includes VPC.

Soojin Lee: I’ll do a pass:
- Long desc structure: “What you get with Hosted API” section + “Also available: Dedicated + Private (separate SKUs)” section.
- Replace “guaranteed” wording.
- Remove HIPAA reference entirely.

Talia Benson: Assignments / next steps
1) Copy edits (AWS listing long desc + bullets + keywords)
Owner: Soojin Lee
Due: EOD tomorrow (so we can resubmit Wed)

2) Security packet deltas (encryption at rest/KMS language + audit logging + retention consistency)
Owner: Marcus Lin (tech wording) + Olga Petrov (compliance-approved phrasing) + Aisha sign-off
Due: draft by tomorrow noon PT; final by EOD tomorrow

3) Retention statement consistency check across: listing FAQ, security FAQ doc, security packet
Owner: Elliot Price + Kira Thompson
Due: tomorrow EOD

4) Screenshot updates + redaction
Owner: Elliot Price (coord) + Connor O’Brien (release check) + Rafael Mendes (sanity on monitoring screenshots)
Due: by Thu noon PT

5) Portal resubmission
Owner: Talia Benson
Target: Thu EOD PT

PartnerPortal Bot: AWS Marketplace Review: Comment added on submission ID #aws-mp-4817: “Please remove unverifiable performance guarantees and clarify which deployment options are included in the purchased offer.”

Rafael Mendes: For “usage/cost breakdown” screenshot: please avoid showing internal metric names. Use the customer-facing “Tokens, Latency, Errors” view, and blur any request IDs.

Ethan Park: Quick heads up: reviewer also asked in the call last week about entitlement activation time. If we can add one line like “entitlements typically activate within X minutes” we need to be careful—right now it’s usually 2–10 min but can be longer.

Soojin Lee: I’d avoid specific numbers in listing, but can add: “Activation is typically within minutes; if delayed, contact support” + link to troubleshooting.

Talia Benson: Works. We should align w/ Support doc anyway.

Dr. Aisha Rahman: Please also remove “ISO certified” language unless we are explicitly stating the scope + current status. If we say anything, it should be “ISO 27001-aligned controls” unless Olga confirms certification status and scope.

Olga Petrov: Confirmed: we should not say “ISO certified” in the listing. We can say “SOC 2 Type II” and “security program aligned with ISO 27001 controls” (approved phrasing). I’ll add to the packet.

Connor O'Brien: Once screenshots are final, drop them in the screenshot inventory doc and tag me. I’ll run through the marketplace review checklist before portal upload.

Talia Benson: Perfect. I’ll keep this thread as the source of truth for AWS feedback items. If anyone hears new reviewer asks, paste them here w/ link/screenshot from portal.
